item.title: Arsenal up to second
item.description: Arsenal are up to second in the Women's Super League after beating Everton 3-1 at Goodison Park. Katie McCabe scored the opener for the Gunners in that game. England captain Leah Williamson made her first appearance since the Euro 2025 final in the summer. Advertisement

item.title: Ireland South MEP calls on government to access EU fund to support Fastway workers
item.description: An Ireland South MEP is calling on the government to to access an EU fund to support Fastway workers who have lost their jobs. The European Globalisation Adjustment Fund for Displaced Workers (EGF) was set up by the European Union to support to workers who have been made redundant as a result of trade liberalisation. The aim of the fund is to allow workers to remain in employment or find a new job quickly, through services including counseling, career advice and several forms of training. Advert

item.title: Seven student members to be awarded by Cara Credit Union
item.description: Cara Credit Union has announced the winners of its Education Awards and Dan Kellegher Memorial Awards. item.title: Liverpool defeat Brighton
item.description: Mo Salah made his Liverpool return in a 2-nil win at home to Brighton in the Premier League. He came on as a substitute in the first half and went on to assist Hugo Ekitike's second goal. Cole Palmer scored for the first time since September as Chelsea beat Everton 2-nil at Stamford Bridge. item.title: Cromane chasing All-Ireland glory; match subject to inspection
item.description: Cromane can tomorrow become national champions. At 2 o'clock they contest the AIB Ladies All-Ireland Junior Club Football Championship final, against Muckalee from Kilkenny in Parnell Park, Dublin. The match is subject to a pitch inspection tomorrow morning and will be moved to Abbotstown if necessary. item.title: 5 in a row for Kilkerrin-Clonberne
item.description: The women of Kilkerrin-Clonberne have claimed a fifth AIB All-Ireland club title in a row this evening. They were too much for St Erg-nat's of Antrim in the decider. The Galway side came out on top by 2-8 to 1-5 at Croke Park. Advertisement Knockbride of Cavan are the intermediate champions. They had no problems in today's final, beating Galway's Caltra Cuans by 3-10 to 4 points.

item.title: Two-time champion survives scare to reach second round
item.description: Two-time champion Gary Anderson survived a scare to reach the second round of the World Darts Championship. He got past Adam Hunt 3-2 at Alexandra Palace - while there were also wins for David Davies, Andrew Gilding and Luke Woodhouse. World number two Luke Humphries takes on Ted Evetts in the evening session. Advertisement
